claim: Amazon S3 File Gateway supports accessing S3 buckets that have S3 Object Lock turned on.
question: Does S3 File Gateway work with S3 buckets that use S3 Object Lock?

evidence.quote: Amazon S3 File Gateway supports accessing S3 buckets that have Amazon S3 Object Lock turned on. Amazon S3 Object Lock allows you to store objects using a "Write Once Read Many" (WORM) model.

claim: With S3 Object Lock on, a file can still be modified, deleted or renamed through an S3 File Gateway share; the gateway then places a new version of the object without affecting the previous, locked version.
question: What happens when a client changes a file whose S3 object is locked by S3 Object Lock?

values.display: places a new version of the object

qualifiers.scope: S3 File Gateway with S3 Object Lock

evidence.quote: If you turn on Amazon S3 Object Lock, you can still modify the object. For example, it can be written to, deleted, or renamed through a file share on a S3 File Gateway. When you modify an object in this way, S3 File Gateway places a new version of the object without affecting the previous version (that is, the locked object).

claim: Bucket policies for lifecycle management, cross-region replication and S3 event notification apply directly to objects stored in the bucket through Storage Gateway.
question: Do S3 lifecycle, cross-region replication and S3 event notifications work with File Gateway objects?

values.display: lifecycle management, cross-region replication, and S3 event notification
apply directly to objects stored in your bucket

evidence.quote: Your bucket policies for lifecycle management, cross-region replication, and S3 event notification, apply directly to objects stored in your bucket through AWS Storage Gateway.

claim: For objects deleted by an S3 lifecycle policy, you need to enable the periodic cache refresh feature or call the RefreshCache API to reflect the deletion to NFS clients.
question: What must you do so NFS clients see objects removed by an S3 lifecycle policy?

values.display: enable the periodic cache refresh feature

qualifiers.condition: objects deleted by a lifecycle policy

evidence.quote: In the case of objects deleted by lifecycle policy, you will need to enable the periodic cache refresh feature or call the RefreshCache API to reflect these changes to your NFS clients.

claim: S3 event notifications for objects written by an S3 File Gateway can arrive for partial files that the gateway created to store data durably, and these partial files may not be application consistent.
question: Why are S3 event notifications unreliable for telling that an S3 File Gateway upload finished?

evidence.quote: If using S3 event notifications you may receive events for partial files created by the gateway to ensure your data is durably stored in S3. Partial files may occur for a number of reasons, such as the gateway needing to free up cache space, or a high rate of writes to a file. These partial files may not be application consistent.

claim: A file upload notification covers each individual file that S3 File Gateway uploads to S3, while S3 event notifications include partial file uploads so they cannot show that a file upload has completed.
question: How is a file upload notification different from an S3 event notification?

evidence.quote: The file upload notification provides a notification for each individual file that is uploaded to Amazon S3 through S3 File Gateway. S3 event notifications provide notifications that include partial file uploads so there is no way to tell from the S3 event notification that the file upload has completed.

claim: S3 File Gateway stores written data locally first and uploads it to S3 asynchronously, and you can request CloudWatch Events notifications when the upload of an individual file completes, to trigger workflows such as a Lambda function.
question: How does an application learn that an S3 File Gateway file reached S3?

qualifiers.condition: the page names CloudWatch Events; EventBridge is the current name of that service

evidence.quote: When you write files to your file share with Amazon S3 File Gateway, the data is stored locally first and then asynchronously uploaded to your S3 bucket. You can request notifications through AWS CloudWatch Events when the upload of an individual file completes. These notifications can be used to trigger additional workflows, such as invoking an AWS Lambda function or Amazon EC2 Systems Manager Automation, which is dependent upon the data that is now available in S3.

claim: When two S3 File Gateways map to the same bucket, files uploaded by the first are not visible to the second because it uses a locally cached version; you can use file upload notification and CloudWatch Events to issue a RefreshCache request on the second gateway.
question: How can a second S3 File Gateway see files that the first gateway just uploaded to the same bucket?

qualifiers.condition: two S3 File Gateways map to the same S3 bucket

evidence.quote: The files upload to Amazon S3, but they are not visible to Gateway2 because it uses a locally cached version of files in Amazon S3. To make the files visible in Gateway2, you can use the `NotificationPolicy` parameter to request file upload notification from Gateway1 to notify you when the upload file is done. You can then use CloudWatch Events to automatically issue a RefreshCache request for the file share on Gateway2.

claim: An SMB file share can be limited to Active Directory users only or offer authenticated guest access, can be read-only or read-write, and can be limited to specific AD users and groups.
question: How do you control who can use an SMB file share on S3 File Gateway?

qualifiers.scope: S3 File Gateway SMB file share

evidence.quote: You can configure your SMB file share to be accessed by Active Directory (AD) users only or provide authenticated guest access to users in your organization. You can further limit access to the file share as read-only or read-write, or to specific AD users and groups.

claim: An NFS file share can be limited to specific NFS clients or networks, set read-only or read-write, and can use user permission squashing.
question: How do you limit access to an NFS file share on S3 File Gateway?

values.display: limiting access to specific NFS clients or networks

qualifiers.scope: S3 File Gateway NFS file share

evidence.quote: You can configure your NFS file share with administrative controls such as limiting access to specific NFS clients or networks, read-only or read-write, or enabling user permission squashing.

claim: You can export an SMB file share with a guest username and password without Active Directory, but you need to change the default password with the console or the service API before you set up the share for guest access.
question: Can an SMB file share be exported without Active Directory, and what must you change first?

qualifiers.scope: S3 File Gateway SMB file share

evidence.quote: You can export an SMB file share using a guest username and password. You will need to change the default password using the Console or service API before setting up your file share for guest access.

claim: Amazon S3 File Gateway integrates with Microsoft Active Directory on premises as well as with in-cloud Active Directory solutions such as Managed Microsoft AD.
question: Does S3 File Gateway integrate with Microsoft Active Directory?

values.display: integrates with Microsoft Active Directory on-premises

evidence.quote: Yes, Amazon S3 File Gateway integrates with Microsoft Active Directory on-premises as well as with in-cloud Active Directory solutions such as Managed Microsoft AD.

claim: To use Active Directory authentication for an SMB file share, you edit the gateway's SMB settings with your Microsoft AD domain credentials, which lets the gateway join the domain and lets domain members access the share.
question: How does an S3 File Gateway SMB share authenticate users with Active Directory?

values.display: gateway to join your Active Directory domain

evidence.quote: To use your corporate Active Directory or AWS Managed Microsoft AD for user authenticated access to your SMB file share, edit the SMB settings for your gateway with your Microsoft AD domain credentials. Doing this allows your gateway to join your Active Directory domain and allows members of the domain to access the SMB file share.

claim: The default SMB security level for S3 File Gateway is Enforce encryption, which enforces both encryption and signing for SMB client connections to gateway file shares. It does not affect traffic from the gateway to AWS, which is always encrypted.
question: What is the default SMB security level of an S3 File Gateway?

qualifiers.scope: S3 File Gateway SMB file shares

evidence.quote: The default security level for S3 File Gateway is **Enforce encryption**. This setting enforces both encryption and signing for SMB client connections to gateway file shares, meaning that all traffic from the client to the gateway is encrypted. This setting does not affect traffic from the gateway to AWS, which is always encrypted.

claim: If security requirements allow a more relaxed posture, you can change the SMB security level to Client negotiated, which disables SMB encryption and enforces SMB signing only; client connections can then use multiple vCPUs, which typically increases throughput.
question: What does the Client negotiated SMB security level change?

qualifiers.scope: S3 File Gateway SMB file shares
qualifiers.condition: you must wait for the file share status to return to Available and reconnect SMB clients for the change to take effect

evidence.quote: If your security requirements allow for a more relaxed posture, you can change the security level to **Client negotiated**, which will disable SMB encryption and enforce SMB signing only. With this setting, client connections to the gateway can utilize multiple vCPUs, which typically results in increased throughput performance.

claim: Storage Gateway uses SSL/TLS to encrypt data transferred between the gateway appliance and AWS storage. By default it uses Amazon S3-managed keys (SSE-S3) to server-side encrypt all data it stores in S3, and you can use the API to configure SSE-KMS instead.
question: How does Storage Gateway encrypt data in transit and at rest by default?

evidence.quote: Storage Gateway uses SSL/TLS (Secure Socket Layers/Transport Layer Security) to encrypt data that is transferred between your gateway appliance and AWS storage. By default, Storage Gateway uses Amazon S3-Managed encryption keys (SSE-S3) to server-side encrypt all data it stores in Amazon S3. You have an option to use the Storage Gateway API to configure your gateway to encrypt data stored in the cloud using server-side encryption with AWS Key Management Service (SSE-KMS) keys.

claim: All data transferred between an S3 File Gateway and AWS storage is encrypted with SSL. By default, all data stored in S3 is encrypted server-side with SSE-S3, and for each file share you can optionally choose SSE-KMS.
question: How does S3 File Gateway encrypt data in transit and at rest?

values.display: encrypted server-side with Amazon S3-Managed Encryption Keys (SSE-S3)

qualifiers.condition: the encryption method is set per file share

evidence.quote: All data transferred between the gateway and AWS storage is encrypted using SSL. By default, all data stored in S3 is encrypted server-side with Amazon S3-Managed Encryption Keys (SSE-S3). For each file share you can optionally configure to have your objects encrypted with AWS KMS-Managed Keys using SSE-KMS.

claim: You can configure the file shares of an S3 File Gateway to encrypt stored objects with AWS KMS-managed keys by using SSE-KMS or DSSE-KMS.
question: Which KMS-based encryption methods can an S3 File Gateway file share use?

evidence.quote: You can configure the file shares on your S3 File Gateway to encrypt stored objects with AWS KMS–managed keys by using SSE-KMS or DSSE-KMS.

claim: When you use an AWS KMS key for server-side encryption with Storage Gateway you must choose a symmetric key; Storage Gateway does not support asymmetric keys.
question: Can Storage Gateway use an asymmetric KMS key?

evidence.quote: When you use an AWS KMS key for server-side encryption, you must choose a symmetric key. Storage Gateway does not support asymmetric keys.

claim: If an S3 File Gateway file share uses SSE-KMS or DSSE-KMS, you must manually add the kms:Encrypt, kms:Decrypt, kms:ReEncrypt*, kms:GenerateDataKey and kms:DescribeKey permissions to the IAM role associated with the file share.
question: Which permissions must the file share IAM role have when the share uses SSE-KMS?

qualifiers.scope: S3 File Gateway file share with SSE-KMS or DSSE-KMS

evidence.quote: If you configure your File Gateway to use SSE-KMS or DSSE-KMS for encryption, you must manually add `kms:Encrypt`, `kms:Decrypt`, `kms:ReEncrypt*`, `kms:GenerateDataKey`, and `kms:DescribeKey` permissions to the IAM role associated with the file share.

claim: After you update the encryption method of an S3 File Gateway file share, the gateway uses the new method for new objects and for stored objects it later updates or modifies; existing S3 objects receive the new method only if the gateway updates or modifies them.
question: Are existing S3 objects re-encrypted when you change the file share encryption method?

values.display: for all new objects it creates
updated or modified by the gateway

evidence.quote: After you update the encryption method, the gateway uses the new method for all new objects it creates in Amazon S3 and for any stored objects that it updates or modifies in the future. Existing Amazon S3 objects will only receive the new encryption method if they are updated or modified by the gateway.

claim: For best performance the S3 File Gateway cache disk size must be tuned to the size of the active working set, and using multiple local disks for the cache increases write performance by parallelizing access to data.
question: What does the Performance page say about S3 File Gateway cache disks?

values.display: tuned to the size of the active
Using multiple local disks for the cache

evidence.quote: For best performance, the cache disk size must be tuned to the size of the active working set. Using multiple local disks for the cache increases write performance by parallelizing access to data and leads to higher IOPS.

claim: S3 File Gateway is not designed to act as a full enterprise NAS replacement: it emulates a file system but is not a file system.
question: Is S3 File Gateway a full replacement for an enterprise NAS?

values.display: not designed to act as a full enterprise

evidence.quote: S3 File Gateway is not designed to act as a full enterprise NAS replacement. S3 File Gateway emulates a file system, but it is not a file system.

claim: Sequential writing from one client is single-threaded, so AWS recommends multiple threads from each NFS or SMB client writing files in parallel, and multiple clients at once, to maximize S3 File Gateway throughput.
question: How do you get the best throughput from an S3 File Gateway?

values.display: multiple threads from each NFS or SMB client
using multiple NFS or SMB clients simultaneously

evidence.quote: Instead, we recommend using multiple threads from each NFS or SMB client to write multiple files in parallel, and using multiple NFS or SMB clients simultaneously to your S3 File Gateway to maximize the gateway throughput.
